## SCHED4 · SCHED4-design — SCHED4: a timeout or deadline is armed on the hart running its payer; the negative's construction; the count gated

Status: **open** · Assigned to: kernel-red-2 · Revision: 5

### K33 implementer 3 · Question

Event: `5ce5ba0b3bb4af49dcdeab5f2812dd36` · 2026-10-15T01:01:47Z

> SCHED4 design for your ruling before I build; the full design is .wash/local/SCHED4-report.md 'Design' (60 lines).
> 
> Rule: per kind, the global earliest item with its payer's id (None on a tie); a timeout's payer is the blocked thread's budget, a deadline's the dying budget's parent. Decided only in rearm(): a hart arms an item unless another hart runs its payer (sched::runner_ids(), O(harts)) and is armed by then; None or a payer running nowhere: every hart, as today. rearm's call sites unchanged; note_* only record (the WIP's extra rearm calls dropped). No deadline scan on the switch path. A one-thread budget's own timeout runs nowhere: unplaced by construction (the measured residual); the gate is about deadlines. Idle harts arm only unplaced items: the latency cost.
> 
> K33: both slice ends re-arm in leave with the post-switch runners; repick's due() keeps the global hints, so an item due that another hart is armed for is still served here through kmain: placement of the interrupt, not an exclusion; hence a bound, not zero.
> 
> Negative: in deadline-flood the creator's own call entries serve most deadlines (91/96), so timer-any-hart lands on the victim only by phase (~1 %). Construction `deadline-placement`: the creator creates its deadlines then spins in user mode without calls, beside an equal spinner victim, 2 harts: any-hart lands many on the victim (~0.19 % of its pool each), B1 none. It gates the count; the recorded negative adds timer-any-hart; deadline-flood-billed-traced and sched-exit-churn gate it too at 2 harts.
> 
> Oracle arg foreign_timer_in=<share>:<per_mille>: interrupts that interrupted the judged budget and charged outside its marks, ticks over the judged budget's charged ticks <= 10; 2+ harts. Latency before/after (sched-latency, kernel-containment, 2 harts, both widths) within one section. Pages timer.md, scheduling.md, testbench.md; no model rule change; three commits.

### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `1c64d0e7d0516c9ef810c704aabf0161` · 2026-10-15T01:03:34Z

> Ruling (kernel-red-2), 1 of 2: build it as designed (the Architect's form: global earliest item + payer id, decided in rearm() only, runner_ids() O(harts), no deadline scan on the switch path; note_* record only). Read the Design, the plan node, time.rs rearm/due. Bindings:
> 
> 1. Liveness invariant, stated in timer.md and host-tested on time.rs's decision (a pure function of hint, payer, runner set, armed[]): at every return to user mode and before every idle, for each kind's earliest item at least one hart is armed at or before it. The fallbacks are part of the rule: payer None or running nowhere: every hart; payer's hart(s) armed later than the item (an item noted on another hart): this hart arms too until the payer's hart re-arms. A tie is two DIFFERENT payers at one instant; children of one parent at one instant share the payer and are placed (deadline-placement may rely on that; say so in its toml).
> 
> 2. due() keeps the global hints (I13: a passed item is served by the first entry anywhere). State in testbench.md that foreign_timer_in counts timer interrupts from user mode only, and have the oracle also REPORT (not gate) the foreign expiry ticks reached on the judged budget's hart through kmain from its slice ends and through its own call entries, so the bound's exclusion is visible, not hidden.
> 
> 3. The gate 10 per mille at 2+ harts is accepted; the recorded negative (timer-any-hart, compiled out by default) must fail deadline-placement on both widths, quoted. deadline-flood-billed-traced and sched-exit-churn gate it at 2 harts as proposed.

### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `43b67e5caba4e339baf1c80eb98afd57` · 2026-10-15T01:13:57Z

> Review of SCHED4 commit 1 (kernel-red-2): OK to build commit 2 on. Base 92b84a5b8, head b2f930729, tree clean. Read: the full diff (time.rs, sched.rs runner_ids, message.rs settle/collect_due, budget.rs 925-948, Cargo.toml, stride Hint + tests, timer.md, scheduling.md, size-budget); time.rs armed[] writes (rearm, expire_due:254, on_interrupt:279).
> 
> Sound: the decision is pure (Hint::due_on), read only in rearm() at its three existing sites, after the switch; note_* record only; the deadline payer is the parent (pf at budget.rs:947; expire_due's fold reads .parent); a tie is two different payers; armed 0 at an interrupt or expiry means "fired, re-arming at the return", and a hart relying on it is covered because every exit re-arms with the runners as they are then: a hart that stops running the payer arms the item itself (payer nowhere, or its other hart armed later) or sees that other hart armed. Liveness holds on that argument; the 20,000-set fixpoint test holds the steady state. timer-any-hart is the plain `at`, test-only. No deadline scan on the switch path. Size lines match.
> 
> P3 (fold into commit 1 or 3; no re-review):
> (a) a host test for the transient: a hart that covered an item switches to another budget and re-arms; the item stays covered, both with the payer now nowhere and with it on a third hart armed later.
> (b) timer.md "R12 for timer work" first sentence ("only if it runs the payer, or no hart does") lacks the third clause (or the payer's hart is not yet armed by then), which the hart-timer paragraph has.
> (c) residuals: add "a destroyed payer whose id is reused before the hint is recomputed" (placement only, bounded).
> (d) every TBD-* in timer.md gone at the package head, numbers measured as ruled.
> 
> Binding 5 stands for commit 2's machine step: sched-timer-entry, wake-no-preempt-harts + twin, sched-latency, kernel-containment at 2 harts re-judged.
